scopeNote: Extended on the lead's instruction from the label/hint pair to the whole field family: migrating Label/HintText alone left the still-React-Aria Input/TextArea without a label association (a11y gate: axe `label` critical on input-invalid and textarea-invalid), because React Aria's label context only participates with React Aria controls. label.tsx and hint-text.tsx are unchanged from the first pass; input.tsx and textarea.tsx are newly migrated so the family wires as one unit (Field.Root + Field.Label + Field.Control/Input + Field.Description + Field.Validity).

semanticDifferences: Field.Label registers the label id the control points at with aria-labelledby, and derives htmlFor from the registered control (LabelableProvider.controlId). React Aria's Label got the same wiring from RAC's LabelContext, which TextField/NumberField/Select fed with react-aria's labelProps. Element, classes and text content are unchanged.

Field.Description publishes its id through LabelableProvider.setMessageIds; Field.Control merges those ids into aria-describedby (useFieldValidation.getValidationProps -> getDescriptionProps) and adds aria-invalid while the field is invalid. React Aria's Text inherited descriptionProps/errorMessageProps from RAC's TextContext slots instead.

Field parts must be inside Field.Root: FieldLabel/FieldDescription/FieldValidity call useFieldRootContext(false), which throws 'Base UI: FieldRootContext is missing' (error 28 in production). Label and HintText therefore branch on the field context: Field.Label / Field.Description inside a Base UI field, an identical-class <label> / <span> outside it, which is how the 43 importers that render them standalone (select-native, pin-input, ...) keep working.

There is no public export for the default field context (internals/field-root-context exports FieldRootContext and useFieldRootContext only), so 'is there a Field.Root above?' is answered with Base UI's own missing-context sentinel: useFieldRootContext(true).setValidityData !== NOOP. Both subpaths are entries of the package's exports map and are pinned to 1.8.0 with the rest of @base-ui/react.

Field.Root (and Field.Item) are the only providers of the label/description context. NumberField/OTPField/Select/Combobox/Checkbox/Radio/Switch only consume it, so a payload Label inside one of those families associates with its control only when the owning component wraps it in Field.Root - the composition Base UI documents for those families.

Field.Description renders a

by default, which would change the hint's element and its inline/block participation. It is rendered through render={} so the hint stays the React Aria's Text rendered, while keeping the description id registration and the field data-* attributes.

Field.Error is deliberately not used for the isInvalid branch: it mounts only while the field reports invalid and swaps its children for the field's own validity message, which would hide the payload's always-rendered hint text. HintText uses Field.Description for both the description and the error message, exactly as RAC's Text carried both ids.

TextField's className/children render state is rebuilt from Field.Root's className state and from Field.Validity (for the render-prop children) so the React Aria contract {isDisabled, isInvalid, isReadOnly, isRequired} survives; Field.Validity is the public render-prop part that exposes validity, and it renders its children inline (no wrapper element).

React Aria's TextField passed its value binding, name, type, inputMode, maxLength, minLength, pattern, autoComplete, autoFocus, enterKeyHint and spellCheck down to the nested control through its field context. Base UI's Field.Root owns no value, so TextField forwards those to the control through the module's own context (controlProps) and merges them under the explicit props of the control - InputBase's/TextAreaBase's own props always win.

React Aria's Group rendered role="presentation" when it sat inside a field (GroupContext) and role="group" standalone; InputBase reproduces that with the presence of its field context. State attributes are Base UI's (data-disabled/data-invalid/data-filled/data-focused/data-dirty/data-touched) instead of React Aria's data-rac pairs; data-input-wrapper and data-input-size stay on the field root because other components select on them.
State is exposed as Base UI data-* attributes instead of React Aria's data-rac + data-* pairs; Label and HintText keep their own data-label/class vocabulary.

Base UI's Input is Field.Control (a thin native <input> that reads Field.Root context for disabled/name/validity and publishes its id to the label), so the payload's InputBase renders the control itself rather than a styled wrapper the field context reaches through React Aria.

Controlled usage is value + native onChange/onValueChange; React Aria's Input onChange was already the native handler, so InputBase's onChange contract is unchanged, while TextField's value-based onChange (React Aria's) is mapped onto onValueChange.

InputBase still renders without a Field.Root (pagination, dropdown search, input-file, input-tags): Field.Control tolerates a missing context (its useFieldRootContext call is optional), so the same control works standalone with no data attributes and no registration.

migrationRecord.publicComponent: Label, HintText, InputBase, TextField, Input, TextAreaBase, TextArea
migrationRecord.existingUntitledUiBehavior: Label renders a <label> flex row carrying data-label="true" (the `label` custom variant and `**:data-label:` selectors depend on it), a conditional brand/error `*` asterisk and an optional tooltip trigger; it accepted htmlFor/id and inherited React Aria's field label wiring. HintText renders a <span> (description or error message) that React Aria slotted into the field's text context. TextField is React Aria's field: a `group` flex column carrying data-input-wrapper/data-input-size, with render-prop state {isDisabled,isInvalid,isReadOnly,isRequired}; InputBase is a `group/input` wrapper (role=presentation inside a field, group standalone, data-disabled/data-invalid) holding the control, icons, tooltip trigger, password toggle and shortcut; Input/TextArea compose label + control + hint and forward value/name/validation through the field.
migrationRecord.canonicalBehavioralContract: label element associated with the field control (htmlFor + control aria-labelledby), required/invalid state driving the asterisk and the hint colour, data-label preserved for conditional visibility CSS, hint rendered unconditionally with the same element/classes and identified to the control with aria-describedby, aria-invalid on the control when invalid, value binding from the field to the control, native form participation (name/required/disabled/readOnly), and every component still working with no surrounding field at all.
migrationRecord.baseUiCompositionChosen: Field.Root (with the payload's className/data-input-* vocabulary) + Field.Label + Field.Control (rendered as <input> through @base-ui/react/input, as <textarea> through render) + Field.Description (render={<span />}), with Field.Validity feeding the React Aria render-prop state; Label/HintText fall back to plain <label>/<span> with identical classes when no Field.Root is above.
migrationRecord.whyNotOneToOne: Base UI splits React Aria's single styled field object into Root/Label/Description/Control parts and moves required/readOnly onto the control, so the field's own props must be re-projected onto the parts (invalid/disabled on Root, required/readOnly on the control, value binding through a module context) while keeping React Aria's prop names, render-prop state shape and DOM class strings. Field.Error is not the isInvalid counterpart of HintText because it is a validity-driven, conditionally mounted message rather than a caller-rendered hint.

publicApiChanges.reason: Base UI resolves className per part from its own state object; neither component used render-prop state.
publicApiChanges.migrationNote: Pass a string. The payload's 43 importers all pass strings or cx(...) results.
publicApiChanges.compatibility: compile-time narrowing only; payload typecheck passes.

publicApiChanges.compatibility: compile-time narrowing only; payload typecheck passes.

publicApiChanges.compatibility: no payload consumer passes elementType; payload typecheck passes.

publicApiChanges.before: slot={isInvalid ? "errorMessage" : "description"} consumed by React Aria's TextContext and rendered as a DOM slot attribute
publicApiChanges.after: no longer set internally; a consumer-passed slot would render as an inert DOM attribute
publicApiChanges.reason: Base UI has no slot routing: Field.Description registers its id in the field's message ids and Field.Control merges them into aria-describedby.
publicApiChanges.migrationNote: The description/error association now follows from being inside a Field.Root rather than from the slot name; isInvalid keeps its styling meaning.
publicApiChanges.compatibility: the only slot usage was HintText's own; no payload consumer and no stylesheet targets [slot=...] (checked in registry + styles).

publicApiChanges.before: not accepted by React Aria's Input/TextArea props (read-only came from the field context)
publicApiChanges.after: accepted (boolean) and applied as the control's readOnly
publicApiChanges.reason: Base UI has no field-level readOnly, so the control carries it.
publicApiChanges.migrationNote: Additive: existing call sites keep using the native readOnly attribute or the field's isReadOnly, both still work.

publicApiChanges.before: string | ((state: InputRenderProps) => string) with {isHovered, isFocused, isFocusVisible, isDisabled, isInvalid}
publicApiChanges.after: string | ((state: InputState | TextAreaState) => string | undefined) with the same five fields
publicApiChanges.reason: Base UI's own className state is {disabled, touched, dirty, valid, filled, focused}; the React Aria field names are rebuilt from it, with hover/focus-visible tracked on the element because Base UI models them as CSS state only.
publicApiChanges.migrationNote: isInvalid = field invalid (explicit prop wins, else valid === false); isFocusVisible comes from :focus-visible at focus time rather than React Aria's modality tracker.
publicApiChanges.compatibility: same shape, same names; no payload call site passes a function.

publicApiChanges.before: React Aria StyleRenderProps allowed a function of the render state
publicApiChanges.reason: Base UI resolves style functions itself from its own state object, which is a different shape.
publicApiChanges.migrationNote: TextAreaBase keeps its own resize-handle CSS variables; no payload call site passes a style function.
publicApiChanges.compatibility: compile-time narrowing only; payload typecheck passes.

publicApiChanges.reason: Base UI exposes hover as CSS state only; no payload call site used them.
publicApiChanges.migrationNote: Use native onPointerEnter/onPointerLeave (still accepted) if hover behaviour is ever needed.
publicApiChanges.compatibility: no payload consumer passes them; payload typecheck passes.

publicApiChanges.before: extends React Aria's TextFieldProps (isDisabled/isInvalid/isRequired/isReadOnly/validate/value/defaultValue/onChange/name/children render prop/className and style render props)
publicApiChanges.after: same prop names re-declared locally; validate is typed with Base UI's return contract (string | string[] | null | void | Promise<...>) instead of React Aria's ValidationError|true
publicApiChanges.reason: React Aria's types cannot stay once the import is gone.
publicApiChanges.migrationNote: validate is Base UI's native-first validator; no payload call site passes validate.
publicApiChanges.compatibility: all TextField/Input/TextArea call sites in the payload typecheck unchanged (input-group, input-payment, input-file, input-tags included).

publicApiChanges.before: React Aria's TextField rendered its div with data-rac, data-disabled, data-invalid, data-readonly, data-required and spread aria-label onto it
publicApiChanges.after: Base UI's Field.Root div with data-disabled/data-invalid/data-touched/data-dirty/data-filled/data-focused, data-input-wrapper and data-input-size; aria-label is applied to the control only
publicApiChanges.reason: Base UI's field state vocabulary; an aria-label on a plain wrapper div labels nothing and makes the control's name depend on a non-label element.
publicApiChanges.migrationNote: data-input-wrapper/data-input-size are preserved because input-number/input-date/select-native and HintText select on them; group state selectors on the field root must use group-data-disabled/group-data-invalid.
publicApiChanges.compatibility: no CSS in the payload selects on the removed RAC-only attributes (checked in registry + styles).

stateSelectorChanges.reason: compiled to .group:is(:where([data-rac])[data-invalid], :where(:not([data-rac])):invalid) *: the data branch needed React Aria's data-rac on the group element and the native branch needs the group element itself to be natively :invalid, which a wrapper div/field root never is. Base UI emits data-invalid on Field.Root and on its controls, so the attribute variant is the live one (verified in a browser: asterisk turns error-coloured from the wrapper's data-invalid alone).
same rewrite; the hint colour now follows data-invalid on the field root.

stateSelectorChanges.from: group-required:block (label.tsx, asterisk fallback when isRequired is undefined)
stateSelectorChanges.reason: the old selector compiled to .group:is([data-rac][data-required], :not([data-rac]):required) *, i.e. the group element itself had to carry data-required (React Aria) or be natively required - impossible for a wrapper div, since Base UI puts required on the control and Field.Root/Field.Control emit no data-required. group-has-required compiles to .group:has(:is([data-rac][data-required], :not([data-rac]):required)) *, which matches the field root that contains a required control, covering the native `required` attribute (verified in a browser: the asterisk becomes visible from the field's required state alone).

the named-group data variant compiles to .group\/input[data-invalid] *; the InputBase wrapper now carries data-invalid itself when the field (or its own prop) is invalid, which is what React Aria's Group did through the field's GroupContext.
same attribute rename for the wrapped-icon reveal.
the field root is a Base UI element that emits data-invalid; the compiled react-aria selector required data-rac or a natively invalid ancestor.
same rewrite for disabled state coming from the field root (Base UI emits data-disabled there).

crossUnitNotes: The `.group` element that the field's label/hint/wrapper sit in is the field root (TextField's Field.Root): it emits data-disabled/data-invalid, so sibling components that style descendants from it must use group-data-disabled:/group-data-invalid: (a plain :invalid/:disabled fallback no longer exists, and a wrapper div can never match it). Sites seen in the payload: input-number.tsx, input-date.tsx, input-tags.tsx, input-group.tsx, select-native.tsx (in-data-input-wrapper:group-disabled:...).

data-input-wrapper and data-input-size are preserved on the field root, so in-data-input-wrapper:* and in-data-[input-size=sm]:* selectors keep working (verified with a Tailwind compile probe: in-data-input-wrapper:group-data-disabled:opacity-100 -> :where([data-input-wrapper]) .in-...:is(:where(.group)[data-disabled] *)).

Components that migrate to NumberField.Root/OTPField.Root/Select.Root/Combobox.Root/Checkbox.Root/Radio.Root/Switch.Root should wrap them in Field.Root so the existing <Label>/<HintText> children keep their htmlFor/aria-labelledby/aria-describedby wiring; Field.Root is the only provider of that context in 1.8.0 and Field parts throw outside it.

The migration harness has no Field.Root-based case of its own for label/hint: its cases (field-label-hint, field-invalid) go through the payload Input/TextArea, which now provide the Field.Root - so the association path is covered by input-*/textarea-*/form-submit. A dedicated Field.Root + Field.Control + Field.Description case would still be the sharper regression test if the lead wants one added to src/migration-harness.tsx (not editable from this unit).

notes: node node_modules/typescript5/bin/tsc -p registry/untitledui/tsconfig.json -> 0 errors for the whole payload, including every consumer of the preserved API: input-group, input-payment, input-file, input-tags, input-tags-outer, pagination, dropdown-search-*, sidebar/header navigation, pin-input, select-native.

a11y gate: node compiler/migration/a11y.mjs --port 5173 --label candidate -> PASS, 43 cases, 0 new violations (the reported input-invalid and textarea-invalid axe `label` criticals are gone; the only remaining violations are the pre-existing slider/nav-account-card ones).

parity gate: node compiler/migration/capture.mjs --label migrated --port 5173 && node compiler/migration/parity.mjs --label migrated -> 0 failures and 0 notes in every input-*, textarea-* and field-* case (13 compared cases include the 7 relevant ones); the 3 remaining failures are modal-open (dialog family, another unit), listed here only so the numbers are unambiguous.

parity detail fixed during the pass: InputBase's trailing-icon padding must stay prop-driven. React Aria's field context never fed `hasTrailingIcon = tooltip || isInvalid` (only the state props), so the first implementation rendered pr-9 for the field-invalid case and the gate caught it as slot input,wrapper padding baseline=8px 12px 8px 12px candidate=8px 36px 8px 12px. Restoring the prop-only expression made the case match.

hydration gate: node compiler/migration/hydration.mjs --port 5173 -> PASS, 43/43 cases hydrated, 0 mismatches (81,721 SSR bytes), so the new Field.Root/Field.Validity structure and the conditional Label/HintText rendering hydrate cleanly.

Behaviour measured in the live DOM (harness page, input-* and textarea-* cases): label -> control association (label for/id, control aria-labelledby), aria-describedby for the hint, aria-invalid plus data-invalid on the control, disabled/read-only propagation, roles unchanged (presentation inside a field, none for textarea), and the captured slot styles equal the React Aria baseline (input: padding 8px 12px, font-size 16px, height 40px, color oklch(0.205 0 none); label: display flex, gap 2px, font-size 14px, font-weight 500, line-height 20px).
